passage: My name is Harsha, and for three months Gargi has messaged me at all hours. Last night her voice note arrived at 1 a.m., and I listened with my eyes half shut because I had a chemistry test at eight. I love her. She told me something heavy about her home and said I was the only one she could trust. But lately I answer with just "hmm" and "ok", and then feel guilty and resentful in the same breath. Today I finally said, "I want to be there for you, but I can't be your only person, and I can't reply after ten." She looked hurt. I suggested her aunt, and the school counsellor too. She said she would think about it.

qa.q: What time did Gargi's voice note arrive last night?
qa.a: Her voice note arrived at 1 a.m.

qa.q: What was Harsha feeling about the late-night messages, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Harsha was worn out and a little resentful while still caring; the "hmm" and "ok" replies and the guilt in the same breath show it.

qa.q: What would you advise Harsha to do if Gargi keeps messaging late at night?
qa.a: Keep the limit kindly, and gently repeat the idea of talking to her aunt or the school counsellor.

qa.q: How might Gargi have felt when Harsha set the limit?
qa.a: Gargi looked hurt, and may have feared losing the one person she trusts, though saying she would think about it shows the idea did not fall on deaf ears.

grounding: Harsha is worn out by a friend's constant heavy confiding, sets a limit and points to a counsellor and family.
